subsystems.name: EEG electrodes and amplifier
subsystems.role: records the brain's electrical activity with millisecond timing.

subsystems.name: NIRS optodes
subsystems.role: shine near-infrared light through the scalp and detect how much scatters back, tracking blood oxygenation.
parts: light sources (LEDs or laser diodes near 760 and 850 nm)

subsystems.name: Hybrid headgear
subsystems.role: holds electrodes and optodes at the same scalp locations without blocking each other.

subsystems.name: Synchronisation electronics
subsystems.role: keeps the fast electrical and slow optical streams on one clock.

subsystems.name: Processing and fusion software
subsystems.role: separates brain signal from artefact and combines the two views.

buildSteps.title: Choose scalp positions
buildSteps.detail: EEG sites follow the standard 10–20 system; optical channels are then fitted into the gaps between electrodes so light and electrical contact don't compete for the same patch of skin.

buildSteps.title: Design the headgear
buildSteps.detail: A flexible cap or custom-printed frame is made to hold each sensor at its assigned position, with light-tight spacing so one source does not leak into a neighbouring detector.

buildSteps.title: Build the optical channels
buildSteps.detail: Emitters at two near-infrared wavelengths are paired with detectors roughly 3 cm away — far enough to reach cortical tissue, close enough for the light to return. Short extra channels at about 1 cm are added to record scalp blood flow for later subtraction.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: A high-impedance, low-noise EEG amplifier is built alongside the NIR source driver and detection chain, with separate sampling rates (electrical activity in the hundreds of hertz, optical signals at tens of hertz).

buildSteps.title: Synchronise everything
buildSteps.detail: A single clock and trigger line stamp both data streams so an electrical spike and the blood-oxygen change it causes can be aligned later.

buildSteps.title: Fit and calibrate on a person
buildSteps.detail: Electrode impedances are checked, optical coupling is adjusted, and the raw signal is inspected for a clean heartbeat trace — the standard sign that NIRS is seeing through to blood vessels.

buildSteps.title: Co-register positions
buildSteps.detail: Sensor locations are digitised or scanned so results can be mapped onto a head model.

buildSteps.title: Acquire and clean data
buildSteps.detail: The recording is corrected for head motion, scalp blood flow is regressed out of the optical channels, and electrical artefacts such as muscle and eye activity are removed.

buildSteps.title: Fuse and decode
buildSteps.detail: Features from both modalities are combined — for example using the fast electrical signal to time-lock the slow vascular one — to produce a brain-state estimate or a control signal.

prerequisites.tech: Near-infrared light sources and sensitive photodetectors
prerequisites.why: cheap LEDs and silicon detectors make wearable optical recording possible.
EEG signals are tiny (microvolts) and are easily buried under noise from the optical emitters.

prerequisites.tech: Dry or comfortable electrode and optode materials
prerequisites.why: gel electrodes give the best signal but are impractical for long or repeated everyday use.
the link between neural firing and the blood-oxygen response is variable across people and brain regions, which limits how confidently the two signals can be combined.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time multimodal signal processing and machine learning
prerequisites.why: fusing two noisy streams fast enough for closed-loop use is done in labs but not yet routine in small devices.

pathway.milestone: research-grade hybrid caps used in cognitive-workload studies, brain–computer interfaces and neurorehabilitation
pathway.unlocks: better localisation than EEG alone and better timing than NIRS alone.

pathway.milestone: wireless, dry-sensor headsets with on-board fusion
pathway.unlocks: monitoring outside the lab — cockpits, classrooms, factories and clinics.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop applications such as attention-aware interfaces and adaptive neurofeedback
pathway.unlocks: systems that respond to a measured brain state in real time.

pathway.milestone: clinical-grade wearable brain monitoring for stroke recovery, epilepsy and sleep
pathway.unlocks: continuous assessment without a hospital bed.
everyday use — contingent on accuracy standards, consent and privacy rules.
